overview: This 640-page file tracks Japanese merchant vessels through consular reports of port calls, routes, cargoes, passengers, and health clearances, mostly from December 1940 to April 1941. Telegrams often appear alongside paraphrases sent to the U.S. Navy. Correspondence also shows how officials refined reporting procedures and considered restrictions on fuel and supplies. Some later 1941 documents are interfiled.
interest: Paired consular reports and Navy paraphrases reveal how shipping intelligence was collected, corrected, circulated, and used in policy discussions.
